verses.text: Some men came down from Judea to Antioch and were teaching the believers: "Unless you are circumcised as Moses taught, you cannot be saved."
Paul and Barnabas strongly disagreed with them and argued with them. So Paul, Barnabas, and some other believers were chosen to go up to Jerusalem to see the apostles and elders about this question.
The church sent them on their way. As they went through Phoenicia and Samaria, they told how the Gentiles had turned to God. This news made all the believers very happy.
When they came to Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church, the apostles, and the elders. They reported everything God had done through them.
Then some of the believers who belonged to the group of the Pharisees stood up and said, "The Gentiles must be circumcised and told to obey the law of Moses."
The apostles and elders met together to think about this question.
After much talk, Peter stood up and said to them, "Brothers, you know that some time ago God chose me from among you, so that the Gentiles would hear the message of the good news from me and believe.
God knows the heart, and he showed that he accepted them by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as he did to us.
He made no difference between us and them, for he made their hearts clean by faith.
So why are you testing God now? Why are you putting a heavy load on the necks of the followers, a load that neither we nor our ancestors were able to carry?
No! We believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they are."
The whole group became quiet as they listened to Barnabas and Paul. They told about the signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.
When they finished speaking, James said, "Brothers, listen to me.
Simon Peter has told us how God first showed his care for the Gentiles by choosing from them a people for himself.
The words of the prophets agree with this. As it is written,
'After this I will return and build again David's fallen tent. I will rebuild what was ruined, and I will set it up again,
so that the rest of humanity may look for the Lord, including all the Gentiles who are called by my name. This is what the Lord says, who does these things.'
These things have been known from long ago.
"So my decision is that we should not make it hard for the Gentiles who are turning to God.
Instead, we should write to them, telling them to stay away from food made unclean by idols, from sexual sin, from the meat of strangled animals, and from blood.
The law of Moses has been preached in every city from long ago, and it is read in the synagogues every Sabbath."

Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to choose some of their own men and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas, called Barsabbas, and Silas, two men who were leaders among the believers.
They sent this letter with them: "From the apostles and elders, your brothers, to the Gentile believers in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.
We have heard that some men went out from us without our permission and troubled you with what they said, upsetting your minds.
So we all agreed to choose some men and send them to you with our dear friends Barnabas and Paul.
They have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So we are sending Judas and Silas, who will tell you in person the same things we are writing.
It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to put any more weight on you than these necessary rules:
Stay away from food offered to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual sin. You will do well to keep away from these things. Goodbye."
So the men were sent off and went down to Antioch. There they gathered the church together and gave them the letter.
The people read it and were glad for its encouraging message.
Judas and Silas, who were prophets themselves, said many things to encourage the believers and make them stronger.
After spending some time there, they were sent off in peace by the believers to go back to those who had sent them.
But Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch. There they and many others taught and preached the word of the Lord.
Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, "Let us go back and visit the believers in all the towns where we preached the word of the Lord, and see how they are doing."
Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark, with them.
But Paul did not think it was wise to take him, because he had left them in Pamphylia and had not kept on with them in the work.
They had such a sharp argument that they went their separate ways. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,
but Paul chose Silas and left, after the believers put him into the care of the Lord's grace.
He went through Syria and Cilicia, making the churches stronger.
